title: Marked presentations and finite Hilbert--Samuel tests
statement: Fix a smooth scheme $Z$ over a characteristic-zero field, a closed embedded $X\hookrightarrow Z$, a level $H\in\mathbf N^{\mathbf N}$ [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-invariant], and a finite ordered list of boundary ideal sheaves [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. A marked datum consists of a smooth closed $N\hookrightarrow Z$, a coherent ideal $I\subset\mathcal O_N$ [pqf-def-coherent], and an integer $b>0$; its ambient cosupport is the image of $\{x\in N:\operatorname{ord}_x I\ge b\}$ [def-trf-marked-ideal-order]. The retaining-level locus is the image of $\{x\in X:H_{X/k}(x)=H\}$. Smoothness, closed immersions and etale maps use [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-etale-morphism]. A smooth-blowup test specifies an ideal center $C$, the actual blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_C Z$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], and scheme-theoretic strict transforms of $X,N$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]; the center is contained in the relevant cosupport and has normal crossings with the ordered boundary, in the adapted-coordinate sense [def-per-adapted-normal-crossings-center] (equivalently etale coordinate subspaces in this smooth characteristic-zero setting). The controlled transform is characterized by $I^\prime(C\mathcal O_{N^\prime})^b=I\mathcal O_{N^\prime}$, using ideal multiplication and powers [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. The other tests are the relative affine line [def-sbc-affine-space], which sums $H$ and appends its zero section, and the blowup of the scheme-theoretic intersection of two distinct labelled boundary components; both use ordinary cartesian pullback of $X,N,I$. Every blowup retains the ordered strict transforms of the old boundary and appends its exceptional ideal. A presentation starts with empty test boundary and has equality of the two cosupports after every finite admissible test sequence, with transforms existing for every allowed next test. Equivalence is agreement of all such finite tests. Define these conditions recursively through depth $n$ and then quantify over all $n$. Smooth pullback is the actual cartesian pullback of $X,N,I$, of the boundary ideals, and of the level after $r$ summations on a relative-dimension-$r$ piece. A minimal envelope at $x$ has defining stalk ideal contained in the square of the ambient maximal ideal; full-envelope maximal order means that $N\to Z$ is an isomorphism and the ideal order equals $b$ throughout cosupport. A common etale comparison identifies the embedded intrinsic germs by cartesian squares, their specified points and retained levels, and every ordered earlier-center ideal by actual ideal pullback; earlier centers do not become the newly started test boundary. A locally constant smooth blowup transition records its center inside $X$, local constancy of the Hilbert--Samuel function there, the ambient blowup, the strict transform and their structure maps. A local presentation at a point of a locally closed embedding is a pointed etale localization carrying a presentation of that point\textquotesingle s intrinsic level. These are supplied data and predicates, with no existence or resolution assertion.
